Element.attribute: As the program moves into implementation, and the change it delivers is introduced to the organization, benefits will start to be realized. For some programs, there may be a delay for benefits to be realized, even to the extent they are only realized after the program shuts down.

It is critical that the data presented to stakeholders around benefits realization is accurate and as timely as possible. Care should be taken to review and validate data inputs and the populated reports prior to publication. Incorrect data being distributed to a large audience can undermine the confidence within the Benefits Realization process and may damage individual relationships. The program should therefore develop an appropriate quality assurance process to minimize the risk of error.

Benefits review is not:

  • A project management review, which focus on variances in time and cost from the project plan
  • A quality or performance review
  • A financial audit
  • A “witch hunt” to allocate blame
To communicate program progress to key stakeholders and sponsors, inform decision making and drive action.
